stem: A gaming backend stores session state by key at very high request rates and needs predictable low-latency lookups without SQL joins.

choices.text: Use Aurora PostgreSQL as the primary session-state system of record.
Use a general-purpose managed MySQL instance with secondary indexes for key lookups.
Use ElastiCache as the durable system of record for session data.
Use DynamoDB as the primary key-value datastore.

rationale: DynamoDB matches high-scale key-based low-latency access patterns without join dependencies. Aurora PostgreSQL and MySQL can serve key lookups, and secondary indexes speed them up, but they remain relational-first approaches for this specific access profile. ElastiCache is an in-memory cache tier, so it is not a durable system-of-record store for session data.
